topic_name: Mirror Halves and the Line of Symmetry

item.question: A blue triangle has a dotted line down its middle. If you fold the triangle along the dotted line, does one half cover the other half completely? Now look at four puzzle pieces joined together with a dotted line through the middle. Are the two sides mirror halves?
steps: Fold the triangle along the dotted line: the halves match exactly.
Fold the puzzle pieces along their dotted line: the bumps and holes on the two sides do not match.
Only an exact match gives mirror halves.
item.answer: For the triangle: yes, one half covers the other exactly, so they are mirror halves. For the puzzle pieces: no, when folded along the line the left half does not exactly fit over the right half.
item.text:

Answer: For the triangle: yes, one half covers the other exactly, so they are mirror halves. For the puzzle pieces: no, when folded along the line the left half does not exactly fit over the right half.

steps: Imagine a vertical line down the middle of each building.
Check that the left side matches the right side.
Clouds have no repeating pattern, so no symmetry.

item.question: Does a square have only one line of symmetry? Take a square piece of paper and, by folding, find all its lines of symmetry.
steps: Fold the square in half vertically, then horizontally.
Fold it along one diagonal, then along the other diagonal.
Each fold makes the two halves overlap exactly, so there are 4 lines.
item.answer: No. A square has 4 lines of symmetry: a vertical fold, a horizontal fold, and the two diagonals.

steps: Draw the vertical line through the middle.

item.answer: B and C go to the positions earlier held by A and D, and A and D go to the positions earlier held by B and C: A takes the place of B, B the place of A, D the place of C and C the place of D.
